newsitem.title: PERU: Gunshots heard inside Peru siege residence.
newsitem.headline: Gunshots heard inside Peru siege residence.

text.p: Gunshots were heard inside the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima on Monday after police staged an armed display, parading past the mansion where Marxist rebels are holding 72 hostages, witnesses said.

At least half a dozen gunshots rang out over five minutes beginning at 4:45 p.m. (2145 GMT). About 200 security forces went on alert and several police dived for cover behind the walls of the residence.

Earlier, four armoured personnel carriers and scores of special forces troops with semi-automatic weapons circled the residence several times in a show of strength while a helicopter hovered overhead.
Rebels shouted at the police in the heavily-armed vehicles and security force members responded with obscene gestures.
The guerrillas then fired off several rounds, which police said were warning shots fired into the air. Minutes later most of the police withdrew from the area.
The rebels have mined and booby-trapped the residence, which they stormed on Dec. 17.
